title: Unexpected interaction between `column.major` and Date `handlers` in `as.yaml()`
description:
In `as.yaml()`, setting `column.major=FALSE` appears to prevent the application of Date `handlers`. For a while, I thought I was specifying my handler functions incorrectly, but I don't believe that is the case. I used these references for the handlers:
- https://github.com/vubiostat/r-yaml/issues/18
- https://github.com/r-lib/ymlthis/blob/15e54ad42ab7c1c10b96490c74e63999149afac1/R/yml.R#L184-L191

I've included a minimal example showing the difference in date handling when `column.major=TRUE` (default) vs. when `column.major=FALSE`. This interaction doesn't appear when using the `verbatim_logical` handler, making the Date behaviour entirely unexpected.

``` r
library(yaml)
library(purrr)

## Working date handling
date_handler <- list(Date = function(x) as.character(x))
my_list <- list(date = as.Date(c("2012-10-10", "2014-03-28")))
yaml::as.yaml(my_list, handlers = date_handler)
#> [1] "date:\n- '2012-10-10'\n- '2014-03-28'\n"
## instead of a list, use tibble and df (with column.major = TRUE by default)
my_tbl <- tibble::tibble(date = as.Date(c("2012-10-10", "2014-03-28")))
yaml::as.yaml(my_tbl, handlers = date_handler) |> cat()
#> date:
#> - '2012-10-10'
#> - '2014-03-28'
## but the date_handler doesn't apply with column.major = FALSE?
yaml::as.yaml(my_tbl, handlers = date_handler, column.major = FALSE) |> cat()
#> - date: 15623.0
#> - date: 16157.0

## Same issue with data.frames
my_df <- as.data.frame(my_tbl)
yaml::as.yaml(my_df, handlers = date_handler)
#> [1] "date:\n- '2012-10-10'\n- '2014-03-28'\n"
yaml::as.yaml(my_df, handlers = date_handler, column.major = FALSE)
#> [1] "- date: 15623.0\n- date: 16157.0\n"

## What if convert the tibble to list first?
# purrr::transpose also does the weird number conversion
purrr::transpose(my_tbl)
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$date
#> [1] 15623
#> 
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]]$date
#> [1] 16157
# but not if you do as.list() first
as.list(my_tbl) |>
    purrr::list_transpose(simplify = FALSE)
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$date
#> [1] "2012-10-10"
#> 
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]]$date
#> [1] "2014-03-28"

# what about logical handlers?
my_tbl$bool <- c(TRUE, FALSE)
verbatim_logical <- function(x) {
    result <- tolower(as.logical(x))
    class(result) <- "verbatim"
    return(result)
}
yml_handlers <- c(date_handler, list(logical = verbatim_logical))
# Logical handlers work fine either way, but dates depend on column.major
my_tbl |> yaml::as.yaml(handlers = yml_handlers, column.major = FALSE)
#> [1] "- date: 15623.0\n  bool: true\n- date: 16157.0\n  bool: false\n"
my_tbl |> yaml::as.yaml(handlers = yml_handlers, column.major = TRUE)
#> [1] "date:\n- '2012-10-10'\n- '2014-03-28'\nbool:\n- true\n- false\n"
```

title: yaml 1.2 support
description:
It would be great if that package could support yaml 1.2, which apparently the definite version and is already 10 years old now (https://yaml.org/spec/). Changes are nicely summarized here: https://perlpunk.github.io/slides.tpcig2018/yamlpp/slide022.html. Unexpected behavior as in https://github.com/viking/r-yaml/issues/5 (see the many cross-references) would wanish.

This would imply to turn away from libyaml because it does not seem they are going to implement that spec soon, an issue pending for more than two years: https://github.com/yaml/libyaml/issues/20. A popular alternative to libyaml in C++ would be https://github.com/jbeder/yaml-cpp, but there are many, also in python.

title: `yaml.load` removes `!expr` even when evaluation is turned off
description:
### Description
I have a use case in which I want to load a `yaml` file containing fields with `!expr` in their values and then rewriting to that file when I add new value. Unfortunately when reading in the file `!expr` is removed (although `eval.expr` field is set to `FALSE`). I'm not sure this is desired behaviour.

### Reproducible Example
Using an example from the package vignette:

```
> doc <- yaml.load("inc: !expr function(x) x + 1", eval.expr=FALSE)
+ 
+ doc
$inc
[1] "function(x) x + 1"
```

### Expected Behavior
```
> doc <- yaml.load("inc: !expr function(x) x + 1", eval.expr=FALSE)
+ 
+ doc
$inc
[1] "!expr function(x) x + 1"
```

Is there a specific reason why function is doing this?

title: Nested Lists Have an Empty Layer
description:
Using the example specification below,
```yaml
unexpected:
  - column_days:
    - "Saturday"
    - "Sunday"
  - column_maternal_age:
    - "less than 10"
    - "greater than 50"
```

 a list is created that requires that requires double indexing.

```r
> read_yaml("test.yaml")
$unexpected
$unexpected[[1]]
$unexpected[[1]]$column_days
 "Saturday" "Sunday"  

$unexpected[[2]]
$unexpected[[2]]$column_maternal_age
 "less than 10" "greater than 50"
```

I expect it to create `unexpected$column_days` and `unexpected$column_maternal_age`, not also `[[1]]` and `[[2]]` empty filler.

description:

title: A colon in an `!expr` block throws an error
description:
I raised [an issue on SO](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79590545/cannot-parse-yaml-header-in-flexdashboard#79590545) I came along when trying to use the `!expr` syntax in my rmarkdown YAML header.

While this compiles w/o any problem:

```lang-yaml
navbar:
   - title: !expr Sys.Date()
     href: "#"
     align: right
```

this throws an error:
```lang-yaml
navbar:
   - title: !expr format(Sys.Date(), "Created on: %Y-%d-%m")
     href: "#"
     align: right
```

After some trial and error, I figured that the colon followed by a space `: ` is the culprit, and I found a workaround by replacing the colon by its Unicode representation:

```lang-yaml
navbar:
   - title: !expr format(Sys.Date(), "Created on\U003A %Y-%d-%m")
     href: "#"
     align: right
```

The least we can do is to highlight this in the documentation.

```
[1] NA

Warning message:
In yaml.load("foo: 9876543219") :
  NAs introduced by coercion: 9876543219 is out of integer range
```

Probably better would be to convert to double in such cases. Doubles can handle without loss of precision values up to 2^52 (or 53; can't remember); or use int64 introducing a dependency on bit64. 

A current workaround for me is: 

```
yaml.load("foo: 9876543219", handlers=list(int=function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x); 
  if (x <= .Machine$integer.max & x >= .Machine$integer.max) as.integer(x) else x
}))
```

title: Preserving folded blocks when rewriting YAML
description:
I'm developing a package that can insert author metadata in YAML header of Quarto files. I do this by rewriting YAML blocks using the following steps:

``` r
# extract YAML from file
yaml.load()
# add new data
as.yaml()
# insert YAML back into file
```

The problem is that some [information are lost](https://www.github.com/arnaudgallou/plume/issues/56) in the process, including folded blocks:

``` r
lines <- "
  bar: >
    Lorem ipsum
    Vivamus quis
"

yaml::yaml.load(lines) |> 
  yaml::as.yaml() |> 
  cat()
#> bar: |
#>   Lorem ipsum Vivamus quis
```

My question is: is there any way to preserve folded blocks in that case? I'm not aware of a special type I can use to target the `>` with a handler.

I'm considering to insert author data in a separate YAML header when my insert function detects complex cases (e.g. the use of custom tags, repeated blocks, comments being dropped due to the libyaml dependency, etc.). I would prefer to do that on rare occasions though.

title: Expressions always evaluated in global environment
description:
Minimum example:
```
foo_fun1 = function() {
  foo = "foo"
  yaml::yaml.load("!expr print(foo)")
}

# will throw error
foo_fun1()

foo_fun2 = function() {
  foo <<- "foo"
  yaml::yaml.load("!expr print(foo)")
}

# will print "foo"
foo_fun2()
rm(list=ls())
```

As you can see, expressions are evaluated in the global environment which is why `foo_fun2` runs and `foo_fun1` doesn't.

This is unexpected (to me) because if anything I'd expect both (i.e. both functions inherit from parents) or neither (i.e. `yaml.load` runs in new environment that doesn't inherit from any environments) functions to work.

title: Properly Require / Convert UTF-8
description:
# Problem Statement

* The parser library `libyaml` requires only UTF-8 strings as input. 
* R will label a string encoding as "unknown" by default.
* There have been complaints about performance when working with large files.
* A default call to enc2utf8(x) before calling this library would ensure that UTF-8 is handled properly, but at the expense of memory and performance in a huge hit.
* This has been discussed in issues #21, #90, #105 and in pull request #91, #107. 
* It must be dealt with on data that is going from R to yaml string and from external string/file to an R object. Both directions.
* It can fail at present two ways--one with a hanging request as libyaml continues to ask for the rest of a never coming UTF-8 character, and a general failure due to not being a valid UTF-8 character.

# Ideas

* Change documentation to reflect that UTF-8 strings are required as input. 
* Automatically convert anything that isn't utf8 or unknown string type.
* Possibly add warning for unknown string type (however, this being the default could be more noisy than useful). Leaning against at present.
* **Make UTF-8 autoconversion an option that defaults to present behavior.**

title: Array of 1 not represented as list in R
description:
When we parse below example with `yaml.load`

```yml
key: value
array1:
  - item
array2:
  - item1
  - item2
```
we get

```r
str(yaml::yaml.load("
key: value
array1:
  - item
array2:
  - item1
  - item2
"))
#> List of 3
#>  $ key   : chr "value"
#>  $ array1: chr "item"
#>  $ array2: chr [1:2] "item1" "item2"
```
I would expect to have the option that makes sure `array1` is a list of 1 in this case, representing it was an array of length 1.

Just as a reference when I do the same thing for `json` in `jsonlite`

```r
str(jsonlite::fromJSON('
{
  "key": "value",
  "array1": ["item"],
  "array2": ["item1", "item2"]
}
', simplifyVector = FALSE))
#> List of 3
#>  $ key   : chr "value"
#>  $ array1:List of 1
#>   ..$ : chr "item"
#>  $ array2:List of 2
#>   ..$ : chr "item1"
#>   ..$ : chr "item2"
```

_Note:_ when using `jsonlite::read_json` the `simplifyVector` argument is set to `FALSE` by default

Could we add a similar `simplifyVector = FALSE` option to force the R object to represent the original structure?

(applies to trestletech/plumber#390 )

title: feature request: `raw=TRUE` in `write_yaml`
description:
Hello!, 

Thanks for the awesome package. I'm currently using it to read/write GitHub Actions (GHA) workflow files in my new R package / GH Action called [`rworkflows`](https://github.com/neurogenomics/rworkflows).

I have a scenario where I have a GHA workflow yaml that has the key "on". Thanks to the `handler` arg I managed to read in the yaml file.

However, I couldn't seem to figure out how to prevent the "on" key being written as `'on':` (in single quotes) instead of `on:` when writing back to disk with `write_yaml`. This is an issue for GHA as their parser doesn't recognize keys with quotes.

After some playing around, I figured out that the solution was substituting the quoted character and then using `file(..., raw=TRUE)`, but this feature isn't currently exposed to users via `write_yaml` (as far as I can tell).

## Reprex

```
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".yml")
yml <- yaml::read_yaml("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neurogenomics/rworkflows/master/inst/yaml/rworkflows_template.yml")
```

### Issue 

```
yaml::write_yaml(yml, path)
```

yaml file looks like:

```yaml
name: rworkflows
'on':
  push:
  - master
  - main
  pull_request:
  - master
  - main
```

### Solution

``` 
result <- gsub(shQuote("on"),"on",yaml::as.yaml(yml))
path <- file(path, "w", encoding = "UTF-8", raw=TRUE)
open(path, "w")
on.exit(close(path))
cat(result, file = path, sep = "")
```

```yaml
name: rworkflows
on:
  push:
  - master
  - main
  pull_request:
  - master
  - main
```

 If it's helpful, I'd be happy to implement the raw arg in `write_yaml` and make a Pull Request. Does that sound ok to you (maintainer[s])?

Thanks!, 
Brian

title: Consider supporting an 'include' directive
description:
In a number of use cases, YAML files are carried over from other, similar files.  An example may be YAML frontmatter for Rmarkdown files: certain formatting aspects (say, particular to an author or institution) are copied around from project to project.  

In other languages, _common_ elements can re-use by means of an `#include somefile` statement.  
And at least one other YAML parser implements this in the context of a [larger system for home automation](https://home-assistant.io/docs/configuration/splitting_configuration).    

This carried over from [here](https://github.com/eddelbuettel/linl/issues/2) and subsequent email discussion.  Having an include directive is yaml is probably easier than attempting to change pandoc or rmarkdown, and the issue really is local to the yaml frontmatter.

/cc @aaronwolen

title: verbatim class is not always handled
description:
In this SO question, https://stackoverflow.com/q/66207086/2554330, the user had an example which included elements like this:

    tab <- list(block = "[]", link = "~")

He wanted to convert it to YAML, with the output looking like this:

    block: []
    link: ~

but of course `as.yaml(tab)` adds quotes:

    library(yaml) # Jan 30 devel version 4788abe3
    cat(as.yaml(tab))
    # block: '[]'
    # link: '~'

In the docs it says, "Character vectors that have a class of ‘verbatim’ will not be quoted in the output YAML document except when the YAML specification requires it.", so I figured a handler that converted characters to class verbatim would do what he wanted.  Indeed, it works for the `link` entry, but not the `block` entry:

    cat(as.yaml(tab, handlers = list(character = function(x) structure(x, class="verbatim"))))
    # block: '[]'
    # link: ~

But clearly the user's desired output is legal YAML, so this looks like a bug in `as.yaml`.

title: reading/writing Ns
description:
It looks like an unquoted N character is unconditionally read as the logical value FALSE. When writing, it is therefore quoted.
Is this really how it should be? I get it that a list that only has Y and N entries could be converted to a logical vector

does not what at least I would have expected. When writing, one gets

alphabet: [A, C, G, T, 'N']

which looks also a bit weird.

title: write_yaml file should default to stdout
description:
I think it's kind of standard (?) for R writing facilities to default to writing to `stdout`. Certainly true for `writeLines` and `write.table`/`write.csv` and we've done it for `fwrite`:

```
x = letters[1:3]
writeLines(x)
# a
# b
# c
write.table(x)
# "x"
# "1" "a"
# "2" "b"
# "3" "c"
write.csv(x)
# "","x"
# "1","a"
# "2","b"
# "3","c"
data.table::fwrite(list(x))
# a
# b
# c
```

So it's unfortunate `write_yaml` doesn't do the same:

```
write_yaml(x)
```

> Error in `write_yaml(x)` : argument `file` is missing, with no default

But of course `write_yaml` does support file connections so the fix would be easy:

```
write_yaml(x, stdout())
# - a
# - b
# - c
```

Happy to file a PR.

```
## $tag
## [1] "value"
```

I'm trying to programmatically update lots of yaml files, and these contain useful comments. It would be helpful to me to be able to preserve them.

[`?yaml.load`](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/yaml/topics/yaml.load) hints that it may be possible to specify a handler function to deal with this, but it isn't clear how exactly to go about it.

Please can you either allow a way to preserve YAML comments  or document the process.

title: Crashes with recent CRAN update
description:
I am seeing crashes with the new release of yaml 2.1.17 on files that were working previously.

```r
download.file("https://docs.docker.com/engine/api/v1.25/swagger.yaml", "swagger.yaml")
# expected md5: 40718ff82a9a20e95bce1fa3bd067f7f
```

Because this contains some very large numbers that I do not want to convert to NA I usually read with a handler (the crash/errors will occur but are harder to spot through the NA coercion warnings)

```r
yaml_handlers <- function() {
  list("int" = function(x) {
    nx <- as.numeric(x)
    if (abs(nx) < .Machine$integer.max) {
      nx <- as.integer(nx)
    }
    nx
  })
```

title: List of lists with one element not parsed correctly
description:
If you have a list which only contains one list, this is returned as a string containing an R expression.

For example:
```
x <- 'a:\n -\n  - b\n  - c\n'
yaml.load(x)
```
returns:
```
$a
[1] "c(\"b\", \"c\")"
```

If a second list is added to the larger list, things work as expected.
```
y <- 'a:\n -\n  - b\n  - c\n -\n  - d\n'
yaml.load(y)
```
returns:
```
$a
$a[[1]]
[1] "b" "c"

$a[[2]]
[1] "d"
```
